concepts.explanation: US constitutional right not to testify against yourself. Invoking it means refusing to answer to avoid self-incrimination.

aliases: you have the right to remain silent
concepts.explanation: The warning US police must give on arrest: the right to silence and to a lawyer. Statements without it may be thrown out.
A court order compelling someone to testify or hand over documents. Ignoring it is contempt of court.
A formal charge that there is enough evidence to put someone on trial for a serious crime.
A group of citizens who hear prosecution evidence in secret and decide whether to charge someone.
Pleading guilty to a lesser charge or for a lighter sentence instead of risking a trial.
A legal demand that a detained person be brought before a court so the detention can be justified.
Lying under oath. A crime in itself, separate from whatever the lie was about.
Disobeying or disrespecting a court, punishable by fines or jail at the judge's discretion.
A court order requiring someone to do, or stop doing, a specific thing.
Sworn out-of-court testimony recorded before trial, used to gather evidence and lock in a witness's story.
A written statement sworn to be true, used as evidence.
The reasonable grounds police need before making an arrest or getting a search warrant.

aliases: tried twice for the same crime
concepts.explanation: The rule that you cannot be tried twice for the same offence after an acquittal.
The deadline after which a crime or claim can no longer be prosecuted or sued over.
One lawsuit brought on behalf of a large group of people harmed in the same way.
The rule keeping conversations between a lawyer and client confidential and out of court.
The first court appearance where charges are read and the accused pleads guilty or not guilty.
A serious crime, typically punishable by more than a year in prison. Less serious crimes are misdemeanours.
A verdict of not guilty. The accused walks free and cannot be retried for that charge.
A trial cancelled before verdict because of a serious error or a deadlocked jury. It can be held again.
One country handing over a suspect to another country to face charges there.
Legal authority to make decisions on someone else's behalf, such as over money or medical care.
Legal work done free of charge for the public good.
A government program giving witnesses new identities and locations to keep them safe from retaliation.
The government's power to take private property for public use, with compensation to the owner.
